history.p: Gade wrote his second violin sonata in the spring of 1849 giving it the opus number 19, which was later allocated to "Aquareller" (NWGW Coll. 09). He revised, however, the third movement in 1850, before sending it to Breitkopf & Härtel for publication, and therefore changed the opus number to 21. But in May 1850 C.C. Lose & Delbanco had published "Tre Digte af C. Hauch" (NWGW Coll. 10) giving it the same opus number.

annot.p: Although the title page states that it is the arrangement for piano and cello with the plate no. 10997, the music inside is the original version for violin and piano with the original plate no. 8270. The last music page also bears this plate no. although it is printed on the verso of the cover. The cover contains both solo parts for violin and cello.
